title: Replying to @Joe Weinberg #sleepnomore #immersive #immersiveexperienc...
transcript: Quick update on sleep no more ticketing. The last couple weeks of performances were not on sale when they announced closing, but now they are. And of course that final weekend has now sold out. There's still good availability for January and December, but worth noting that like I said in that comment, last week I paid $138, which was the lowest ticket price they had available for any date. And that was specifically weeknights before and after the holidays. But if you look at some of those same days, that lowest ticket price via dynamic pricing has been bumped up to a hundred and fifty dollars and fifty cents. And a lot of these earliest entry times, of course, are the ones that are gonna sell out the fastest. Yeah, unfortunately I was kind of expecting that to happen. Uh, that's why I bought a ticket last week. And I would not be surprised if prices continue to rise. Despite what some people in my comments said, $150, even $138 is a lot of money to a lot of people, including me. I have seen people point out that $150 is like a pretty standard ticket price for Broadway, and while I would not personally pay that much for a Broadway show, it's true that that is a pretty standard ticket price. And arguably for something like Sleep No More, you do get more bang for your buck because of how much of a unique, immersive experience it is.
classificationReason: Explicitly a 'Replying to @Joe Weinberg' follow-up video providing ticketing/pricing updates for Sleep No More. Primary purpose is responding to prior video's comments, not reviewing a listed production.
